/-!
# Erdős Problem 52

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/52](https://www.erdosproblems.com/52)
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Pointwise

namespace Erdos52

/--
Let $A$ be a finite set of integers. Is it true that for every $\epsilon>0$
$\max( \lvert A+A\rvert,\lvert AA\rvert)\gg_\epsilon \lvert A\rvert^{2-\epsilon}?$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_52 : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → ε < 1 → ∃ (C : ℝ), 0 < C ∧ ∀ (A : Finset ℤ),
    (max (A + A).card (A * A).card : ℝ) ≥ C * (A.card : ℝ) ^ (2 - ε) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): Add additional material.

end Erdos52

reformulations.difference: Lean restricts ε to 0 < ε < 1, whereas the source says every ε > 0. This is equivalent to the source's usual nonempty-set/asymptotic formulation, not a weakening of the conjecture.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a nonempty finite set, n = |A| ≥ 1 and |A+A| ≥ n. Thus, whenever ε ≥ 1, n^(2−ε) ≤ n ≤ max(|A+A|,|AA|), so the omitted range holds unconditionally with C = 1. The range 0 < ε < 1 is precisely the substantive conjecture. Conversely, a bound for all positive ε on nonempty sets extends to the empty set in this restricted range because 2−ε > 1 and 0^(2−ε) = 0. The equivalence between the file's right-hand side and the all-positive-ε statement on nonempty finsets was proved as restricted_iff_allEpsilon in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without using the conjecture or any sorry.
